headline: AI designed genetic blueprints for microscopic viruses in 2025, creator Samuel King to discuss
summary: Stanford PhD student Samuel King, an MIT Technology Review Innovator Under 35, used generative AI to propose genetic blueprints for microscopic viruses in 2025. He will discuss his work in a live conversation.
details: In 2025, Stanford University PhD student Samuel King utilized a generative AI model to propose genetic blueprints for microscopic viruses. This marked a preliminary step towards AI-generated life forms, though not yet a full example.
King, recognized as one of MIT Technology Review's Innovators Under 35, will engage in a subscriber-only conversation. He will discuss his pioneering work and new perspectives on biology.
The live event is scheduled for October 16th at 18:30 BST / 1:30pm EDT / 10:30am PDT. Senior AI reporter James O'Donnell will interview King during the roundtable.

Despite advancements like AlphaGo, current AI agents still lack the creativity for genuinely innovative, open-ended AI research. Breathless claims about AGI and new capabilities often fall apart under scrutiny, highlighting the nuanced progress in the field.
caption:
In 2025, Stanford PhD student Samuel King used generative AI to propose genetic blueprints for microscopic viruses. He's discussing this groundbreaking work live.

In 2025, Stanford University PhD student Samuel King utilized a generative AI model to propose genetic blueprints for microscopic viruses. This marked a preliminary step towards AI-generated life forms, though not yet a full example.

King, recognized as one of MIT Technology Review's Innovators Under 35, will engage in a subscriber-only conversation. He will discuss his pioneering work and new perspectives on biology.

The live event is scheduled for October 16th at 18:30 BST / 1:30pm EDT / 10:30am PDT. Senior AI reporter James O'Donnell will interview King during the roundtable.

Despite advancements like AlphaGo, current AI agents still lack the creativity for genuinely innovative, open-ended AI research. Breathless claims about AGI and new capabilities often fall apart under scrutiny, highlighting the nuanced progress in the field.
